Reproduction Procedure: 1. Assign DA_Architecture_Analyst permission set to a non-admin Salesforce user. 2. Log in as that user. 3. Navigate to Dependency Analyzer and invoke DAUserPreferenceController.getUserPreference or saveUserPreference, or DAAnnotationController.getAnnotations.
Expected Result: Queries and DML executed WITH USER_MODE and 'as user' succeed based on object and field permissions.
Actual Result: Execution fails immediately with System.QueryException ('No such column on entity...') and System.DmlException.
Evidence: Permission set XML contains 0 <fieldPermissions> for DA_User_Preference__c and DA_Annotation__c custom fields.
User/Business Impact: All standard users cannot view or save preferences or annotations. The application completely crashes on startup for non-admin users.
Recommended Fix: Add all required <fieldPermissions> for DA_User_Preference__c and DA_Annotation__c custom fields to DA_Architecture_Analyst.permissionset-meta.xml.

Reproduction Procedure: 1. Open two browser tabs with different projects (Project A in Tab 1, Project B in Tab 2). 2. In Tab 1, select a node to open Investigation Drawer. 3. Detach drawer. 4. Click a neighbor node in Tab 1's detached drawer.
Expected Result: Only Tab 1 should update; Tab 2 should ignore cross-tab messages belonging to Project A.
Actual Result: Tab 2 processes the BroadcastChannel message and attempts to load Project A's node inside Project B context.
Evidence: Code uses BroadcastChannel('da_investigation_channel') without checking event.origin or matching active projectId.
User/Business Impact: Cross-tab state leakage and confusing data display when users work with multiple projects simultaneously.
Recommended Fix: Include projectId and unique session/tab tokens in BroadcastChannel payloads; ignore messages that do not match the active project.

Actual Result: Returns hardcoded mock AccountController and Account nodes without authorization checks.

Reproduction Procedure: 1. Invoke getAnalysisRuns with an invalid state that triggers an internal exception. 2. Observe the AuraHandledException message.
Expected Result: Exception message should be user-friendly without exposing internal stack or system details.
Actual Result: Exposes raw ex.getMessage() concatenated directly into the AuraHandledException.
Evidence: AuraHandledException('Failed to retrieve analysis runs: ' + ex.getMessage())
User/Business Impact: Potential leakage of internal query structures or database state to client-side logs.
Recommended Fix: Log full internal details to an internal logging framework and return a sanitized user-facing error message.
